newsitem.title: UK: New group to subsidise UK digital satellite boxes.
newsitem.headline: New group to subsidise UK digital satellite boxes.

text.p: A new company is to be formed to subsidise the sale of digital satellite decoder boxes in the UK, BSkyB chief executive Sam Chisholm said on Wednesday.
Chisholm said that the jointly-owned company would subsidise the boxes and give all the partner companies involved in digital satellite technology a way into the range of markets it offers.
He said the target price for digital satellite receiver/ decoder boxes was "somewhere in the order of 200 pounds".
Chisholm did not name the partners, but BSkyB is reported to have had talks with British Telecommunications Plc, Japanese electronics company Matsushita and bank HSBC.
BSkyB is planning a digital satellite box with an interactive capacity and allowing the development of services such as home shopping and home banking.
HSBC owns Britain's Midland Bank as well as First Direct, one of the country's oldest telephone banking operations.
"We'll go straight off with the box that will have all the bells and whistles," Chisholm told a news conference.
BSkyB is set to order up to one million digital decoders from four manufacturers as it pushes ahead with plans for a launch later this autumn.
The company has teamed up with Carlton Communications and Granada Group to apply for licences to run digital terrestrial television (DTT) services when they begin in mid-1998.
Chisholm said a "sidecar" adaptor could be fitted to its satellite box to allow it to receive DTT services. The adaptor would probably cost about 100 stg.
He said DTT-specific decoder boxes were likely to cost about 300 stg as the level of subsidy was likely to be lower than for the satellite boxes.
